P01.name: Creating polysemous elements
P01.description: An ontology element (class, property) whose identifier has multiple meanings, representing more than one concept.
P01.how_to_fix: Split the polysemous element into separate, clearly-named elements — one per concept. Use rdfs:label for human-readable names and rdfs:comment to disambiguate.

P02.name: Creating synonyms as classes
P02.description: Several classes whose identifiers are synonyms are created and declared as equivalent, generating a redundant hierarchy.
P02.how_to_fix: Merge synonym classes into one class and use rdfs:label for alternative names. Remove the redundant equivalent declarations.

P03.name: Creating the relationship 'is' instead of using OWL primitives
P03.description: A relationship named 'is' is created instead of using rdfs:subClassOf, rdf:type, or owl:sameAs.
P03.how_to_fix: Replace the 'is' relationship with the appropriate OWL primitive: rdfs:subClassOf for class hierarchy, rdf:type for instantiation, or owl:sameAs for identity.

P04.name: Creating unconnected ontology elements
P04.description: Ontology elements (classes or properties) that are isolated with no relationship to the rest of the ontology.
P04.how_to_fix: Connect isolated elements via rdfs:subClassOf, domain/range assertions, or remove them if they are unused placeholders.

P05.name: Defining wrong inverse relationships
P05.description: Two relationships are defined as inverse of each other when they are not semantically inverse.
P05.how_to_fix: Verify that if property P holds between A and B, the declared inverse Q holds between B and A in all cases. Remove incorrect owl:inverseOf assertions.

P06.name: Including cycles in class hierarchy
P06.description: A cycle appears in the class hierarchy: class A has subclass B, while B is a superclass of A (directly or indirectly).
P06.how_to_fix: Break the cycle by removing one of the rdfs:subClassOf links. If the classes are truly equivalent, use owl:equivalentClass instead.

P07.name: Merging different concepts in the same class
P07.description: A single class whose name refers to multiple distinct concepts that should be modelled separately.
P07.how_to_fix: Split the class into separate classes, one per concept. Establish the appropriate relationship (hierarchy, association) between them.

P08.name: Missing annotations
P08.description: Ontology elements lack human-readable annotations such as rdfs:label, rdfs:comment, or similar documentation properties.
P08.how_to_fix: Add rdfs:label and rdfs:comment annotations to all classes and properties. Consider adding multilingual labels where appropriate.

P09.name: Missing domain information
P09.description: Required domain knowledge is not captured in the ontology, making it incomplete for its intended use case.
P09.how_to_fix: Identify the missing domain concepts through requirements analysis and add the necessary classes, properties, and axioms.

P10.name: Missing disjointness
P10.description: Classes or properties that should be mutually exclusive lack owl:disjointWith or owl:AllDisjointClasses declarations.
P10.how_to_fix: Add owl:disjointWith axioms between classes that cannot share instances. Use owl:AllDisjointClasses for groups of mutually exclusive classes.

P11.name: Missing domain or range in properties
P11.description: Object or datatype properties are defined without specifying their rdfs:domain or rdfs:range.
P11.how_to_fix: Add rdfs:domain and rdfs:range declarations to all properties. Ensure they are not overly restrictive (see P18).

P12.name: Equivalent properties not explicitly declared
P12.description: Two or more properties with identical semantics exist but lack an owl:equivalentProperty declaration.
P12.how_to_fix: Either merge duplicate properties into one, or declare owl:equivalentProperty between them if both must be retained for compatibility.

P13.name: Inverse relationships not explicitly declared
P13.description: Relationships that are inverses of each other are not linked via owl:inverseOf.
P13.how_to_fix: Add owl:inverseOf declarations between property pairs that are semantic inverses (e.g., hasParent / hasChild).

P14.name: Misusing owl:allValuesFrom
P14.description: A universal restriction (owl:allValuesFrom) is used where an existential restriction (owl:someValuesFrom) is intended.
P14.how_to_fix: Replace owl:allValuesFrom with owl:someValuesFrom when the intent is 'there exists at least one' rather than 'all values must be'.

P15.name: Using 'some not' in place of 'not some'
P15.description: The quantifier and negation are misplaced, changing the logical meaning (existential with negation vs. negated existential).
P15.how_to_fix: Review the logical intent: 'some not X' means at least one non-X exists; 'not some X' means no X exists. Correct the axiom to match the intended semantics.

P16.name: Using primitive class instead of defined class
P16.description: A class has only necessary conditions (primitive) when it should also have sufficient conditions (defined) for automated classification.
P16.how_to_fix: Add owl:equivalentClass with the defining conditions to make the class defined, enabling reasoner-based automatic classification.

P17.name: Overspecializing the hierarchy
P17.description: Leaf classes in the hierarchy are defined without any instances, suggesting over-engineering of the class structure.
P17.how_to_fix: Remove overly specific leaf classes and represent those distinctions as property values or individuals instead.

P18.name: Overspecializing the domain or range
P18.description: Domain or range definitions are too restrictive, preventing valid usage of the property in broader contexts.
P18.how_to_fix: Generalize the domain/range to a higher-level class, or remove explicit domain/range and rely on local restrictions (owl:someValuesFrom) on specific classes.

P19.name: Defining multiple domains or ranges in properties
P19.description: Multiple rdfs:domain or rdfs:range statements on a property create an implicit intersection, not a union as often intended.
P19.how_to_fix: If union is intended, define a single domain/range as owl:unionOf the target classes. If intersection is intended, verify this is correct semantically.

P20.name: Misusing ontology annotations
P20.description: Annotation property values are swapped or incorrectly used (e.g., description in label field, label in comment field).
P20.how_to_fix: Review annotations: rdfs:label for short names, rdfs:comment for longer descriptions, and use appropriate Dublin Core or SKOS properties for other metadata.

P21.name: Using a miscellaneous class
P21.description: A class is created solely to group non-conforming instances that do not fit elsewhere (e.g., 'Other', 'Miscellaneous').
P21.how_to_fix: Remove the catch-all class. Either refine the existing hierarchy to accommodate the instances, or leave them unclassified at the parent level.

P22.name: Using different naming conventions in the ontology
P22.description: Inconsistent naming conventions are used (e.g., mixing CamelCase, underscores, hyphens across different elements).
P22.how_to_fix: Adopt a consistent convention: UpperCamelCase for classes, lowerCamelCase for properties. Refactor existing names to conform.

P23.name: Duplicating a datatype already provided by the implementation language
P23.description: Classes or individuals are created to represent datatypes that already exist in XSD or the OWL datatype map.
P23.how_to_fix: Replace the custom datatype class with the appropriate XSD datatype (xsd:string, xsd:integer, xsd:dateTime, etc.) in datatype property ranges.

P24.name: Using recursive definitions
P24.description: An ontology element is used in its own definition (e.g., a class defined in terms of itself).
P24.how_to_fix: Break the recursion by introducing an intermediate concept or rephrasing the axiom to avoid self-reference.

P25.name: Defining a relationship as inverse to itself
P25.description: A property is declared as owl:inverseOf itself, which is only valid for symmetric properties.
P25.how_to_fix: If the property is symmetric, declare it as owl:SymmetricProperty and remove the self-inverse. Otherwise, define a proper separate inverse property.

P26.name: Defining inverse relationships for a symmetric one
P26.description: A symmetric property (owl:SymmetricProperty) is redundantly given an explicit owl:inverseOf declaration.
P26.how_to_fix: Remove the owl:inverseOf declaration — symmetric properties are their own inverse by definition.

P27.name: Defining wrong equivalent properties
P27.description: Properties declared as owl:equivalentProperty do not actually have the same semantics.
P27.how_to_fix: Remove incorrect equivalence declarations. If properties are related but not identical, use rdfs:subPropertyOf instead.

P28.name: Defining wrong symmetric relationships
P28.description: A non-symmetric relationship is declared as owl:SymmetricProperty (e.g., 'hasParent' declared symmetric).
P28.how_to_fix: Remove the owl:SymmetricProperty declaration. Only properties where P(A,B) always implies P(B,A) should be symmetric.

P29.name: Defining wrong transitive relationships
P29.description: A non-transitive relationship is declared as owl:TransitiveProperty.
P29.how_to_fix: Remove the owl:TransitiveProperty declaration. Verify that if P(A,B) and P(B,C) then P(A,C) truly holds in all cases before declaring transitivity.

P30.name: Equivalent classes not explicitly declared
P30.description: Two or more classes with the same intended meaning exist without an owl:equivalentClass declaration.
P30.how_to_fix: Either merge the duplicate classes into one, or add owl:equivalentClass if both URIs must be retained for backward compatibility.

P31.name: Defining wrong equivalent classes
P31.description: Classes declared as owl:equivalentClass do not actually denote the same set of instances.
P31.how_to_fix: Remove the incorrect owl:equivalentClass assertion. Use rdfs:subClassOf if one is a specialization of the other.

P32.name: Several classes with the same label
P32.description: Multiple classes share the same rdfs:label value, making them ambiguous to human readers and tools.
P32.how_to_fix: Give each class a unique, descriptive rdfs:label. Use qualifiers or context to distinguish similar concepts.

P33.name: Creating a property chain with a single property
P33.description: An owl:propertyChainAxiom is defined with only one property in the chain, which is equivalent to rdfs:subPropertyOf.
P33.how_to_fix: Replace the property chain with a simple rdfs:subPropertyOf assertion, or add the missing second property to the chain.

P34.name: Untyped class
P34.description: A resource is used as a class (appears as subject of rdfs:subClassOf, etc.) but lacks an explicit rdf:type owl:Class declaration.
P34.how_to_fix: Add an explicit 'rdf:type owl:Class' (or rdfs:Class) triple for the resource.

P35.name: Untyped property
P35.description: A resource is used as a property but lacks an explicit rdf:type declaration (owl:ObjectProperty, owl:DatatypeProperty, or rdf:Property).
P35.how_to_fix: Add an explicit type declaration: owl:ObjectProperty for object properties, owl:DatatypeProperty for data properties.

P36.name: URI contains a file extension
P36.description: The ontology URI includes a file extension (.owl, .rdf, .ttl) making it format-dependent and fragile.
P36.how_to_fix: Use an extension-free URI for the ontology namespace. Serve different formats via content negotiation at that URI.

P37.name: Ontology not available on the Web
P37.description: The ontology or its documentation is not accessible at the declared namespace URI.
P37.how_to_fix: Publish the ontology at its declared namespace URI with proper content negotiation (RDF for machines, HTML for humans).

P38.name: No OWL ontology declaration
P38.description: The file lacks an owl:Ontology declaration with metadata (version, imports, annotations).
P38.how_to_fix: Add an owl:Ontology declaration with at minimum rdfs:label, owl:versionInfo, and dc:creator metadata.

P39.name: Ambiguous namespace
P39.description: Neither the ontology URI nor xml:base is declared, making element URIs ambiguous.
P39.how_to_fix: Declare an explicit ontology URI and set xml:base (or @base in Turtle) to establish a clear namespace for all local names.

P40.name: Namespace hijacking
P40.description: Terms from external namespaces are referenced but are not actually defined in those namespaces.
P40.how_to_fix: Only reference terms that are actually defined in external ontologies. Import the external ontology (owl:imports) or define the term locally.

P41.name: No license declared
P41.description: The ontology metadata does not include any license information, making reuse rights unclear.
P41.how_to_fix: Add a dcterms:license or cc:license annotation to the owl:Ontology declaration pointing to the chosen license URI.
